messages:
Maya (support): FYI incoming ticket from Acme — they see inconsistent routing, some requests hitting eu-west despite client saying us-west. low severity but customer sees higher tail latency.
Alex (infra): Can you paste the raw request/headers they sent?
Maya (support): Customer provided a curl sample, paste below. they say their frontend sends header via a proxy.
Maya (support): ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -H "X-Client-Region: us-west, " https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```
Maya (support): They also included a copy of their nginx proxy which forwards headers as-is.
Ryan (oncall): That header looks like a trailing comma — could be split into two header values by some proxies. If router picks first value and it's empty, it could default to EU fallback.
Emma (devex): Quick check — our edge router expects a single token, and we treat multi-value headers as comma-separated list, taking the first non-empty trimmed token. But if proxy turns it into two separate headers (one empty), ordering can change.
Maya (support): I pulled the request-id from customer logs: req-0a12b3c4. Router logs below (sanitized):
Maya (support): ```[2025-11-18T14:12:03Z] req=req-0a12b3c4 src=10.2.3.4 header.X-Client-Region="" decided_region=eu-west fallback_reason=empty_client_region```
Sasha (eng-runtime): Hmm router saw an empty header. Need to know if proxy inserts an empty header value or if the SDK is emitting an empty header first.
Maya (support): Customer says they use our JS SDK behind a custom CDN edge. They shared SDK request snippet: ```await client.generate({..., region: 'us-west' }) // client adds header: X-Client-Region: 'us-west'``` They claim the CDN adds a trailing comma to support multi-region lists.
Alex (infra): Can customer try a raw curl directly to our edge (bypassing proxy) and confirm region? If raw direct routes to us-west then it's proxy behavior.
Maya (support): Customer ran direct curl and got us-west. With CDN it goes to eu-west.
Ryan (oncall): Repro steps sound clear. Likely their CDN rewrites header to a multi-value with an empty item first, or inserts an extra "" header. Our router code currently does naive first-value selection.
Emma (devex): Short-term support workaround: ask them to ensure header has no trailing comma and to trim values on the CDN. Also they can set region via query param `?region=us-west` which we currently prioritize over header.
Maya (support): I suggested query param workaround and they want an engineered fix so they don't have to change CDN behavior.
Sasha (eng-runtime): I'll triage. Possible fixes: 1) coalesce multiple X-Client-Region header values and choose first non-empty trimmed token; 2) prefer query param if present (we already do but maybe priority ordering bug); 3) log the raw header array for debugging. I can prototype a patch to normalization logic.
Alex (infra): Also add telemetry when header parsing yields empty token so support can surface affected customers.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled for canary to edge-router-staging at 2025-11-19T02:00:00Z (sha: a1b2c3).
Sasha (eng-runtime): I'll open ENG-3812 and attach repro from Acme. ETA: small patch + canary rollout in 24h.
Maya (support): Customer accepted query param workaround for now. They asked for an advisory we can send to their ops team explaining cause and recommended CDN config.
Emma (devex): I'll draft a one-paragraph advisory: explain trailing-comma/multi-value header behavior, recommend trimming/ensuring single token or set region via query param, and note upcoming router normalization fix.
Maya (support): tagging for follow-up: @Sasha please add me to ENG-3812 for status updates.
Sasha (eng-runtime): Will do. thanks. :thumbsup:
Ryan (oncall): Marking this as resolved support side once fix is in canary and advisory sent. :eyes:
Maya (support): Closing loop with customer after canary.
